findings.desc: quality-duplication: runtime-environment-checks.ts:791-800 (resolveCanonicalCoreRoot) duplicates the exact git-worktree-list-porcelain-parsing loop already implemented in resolveCanonicalSelfCoreRoot at runtime-environment-checks.ts:761-770 (identical 9-line block: split into records, find worktree/branch lines, match branch===refs/heads/main, build candidate=join(worktree,packages,main), return realpath if exists). This copies rather than shares the parsing logic the story explicitly set out to mirror. A future fix to the parsing (CRLF handling, detached-HEAD worktree rows, path separators) would need to land in two places and could silently drift apart since nothing enforces they stay in sync. Recommend extracting a shared helper (e.g. findMainBranchWorktreeRoot(anchorDir): string | null) that both functions call, each applying their own already-different fallback semantics on top.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit b9f2786fb5: extracted findMainWorktreeCoreRoot as the single git-worktree-list parsing source; resolveCanonicalSelfCoreRoot and resolveCanonicalCoreRoot now share it and keep only their distinct fallbacks. tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs and validation-protocol-smoke both green after the refactor.

findings.desc: quality-comment-accuracy: runtime-environment-checks.ts:786 comment ("Any git failure falls back to today's un-canonicalized path") and decision.json preMortem[0].mitigation ("Fall back to the current un-canonicalized corePackageRoot on any git failure (behavior identical to today)") both misdescribe the actual fallback. resolveCanonicalCoreRoot's fallback at runtime-environment-checks.ts:788 is `safeRealpath(coreRoot) ?? resolve(coreRoot)`, which DOES apply realpath (symlink-dereferencing) canonicalization. Pre-fix, this branch used `context.corePackageRoot` directly with zero realpath resolution (see pre-diff line 228: `expected = context.corePackageRoot`), so the fallback is not byte-identical to pre-fix behavior as claimed -- it is a new canonicalization step applied even when git fails. In practice this looks benign or even corrective (it keeps `expected` consistent with `globalRealpath`, which is already realpath'd, so it plausibly fixes a latent false-warn for symlinked corePackageRoot paths that the non-git branch previously had), but the comment/decision text asserting behavioral identity to today is inaccurate and could mislead a future maintainer relying on it while debugging a fallback-path anomaly. Recommend correcting the comment/decision text to describe what the fallback actually does (realpath the coreRoot itself, not a byte-identical carry-over of the pre-fix raw-path behavior).
findings.resolvedReason: Commit b9f2786fb5: comment rewritten to state the truth — the non-self fallback is the realpath-normalized core root BY DESIGN (the comparison target globalRealpath is itself realpath-resolved, so symlink normalization must match on both sides), explicitly not a byte-identical pre-fix path. The decision.json preMortem wording inaccuracy is superseded by this code-level statement of record.

findings.desc: quality-orphaned-test: packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs (new file, 3 scenarios) is not wired into any executable test surface. It is not referenced by any packages/main/package.json or root package.json script; the root aggregate "test" script (package.json) does not invoke it; "test:all"/"test:legacy" (run-all-smokes.js, packages/main/src/tasks/run-all-smokes.ts:97/123-127) only discovers files matching *-smoke.js under packages/main/dist/tasks, so a tests/*.mjs file is invisible to it; and validate.ts has no generic tests/*.test.mjs discovery. This breaks the established convention in this same directory: the sibling packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs IS wired via an explicit "test:milestone-status" script (packages/main/package.json) that is itself included in the root aggregate "test" chain. Consequence: this test -- the only automated coverage for the adversarial different-clone-still-warns and non-git-fallback scenarios required by decision.json preMortem 2 -- was run once manually (per the CHK-001 verificationEvidence entries, command: "node packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs") but will not run again on any future regression to resolveCanonicalCoreRoot/resolveCanonicalSelfCoreRoot; "npm test" being green (the checklist's stated acceptance signal) does not actually exercise this file. Recommend adding a package.json script (e.g. test:global-core-realpath) mirroring test:milestone-status and including it in the root aggregate test chain.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit b9f2786fb5: wired per the milestone-status sibling convention — packages/main script test:global-core-realpath (node tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs), root delegating script, and insertion into the root npm test chain right after test:milestone-status. Full npm test exits 0 from the worktree with the new suite in the chain. package.json edits scope-acknowledged.

findings.desc: CHK-001:happy:1 (must, npm run test:brief-output green from inside a story worktree) is not currently reproducible. Re-ran node packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs (pass), npm --prefix packages/main run build (clean rebuild), then npm run test:brief-output from this worktree twice: both runs FAIL with AssertionError doctor brief under budget, got 20606 (budget 20000), at packages/main/dist/tasks/brief-output-smoke.js:380. Debug instrumentation on a copy of the smoke script (scratchpad only, no worktree files touched) shows the targeted fix itself is not regressing: the global-core-realpath check in the fixture doctor brief renders ✓ (pass) with no Relink or reinstall text (CONTAINS_RELINK=false). The overage instead comes from unrelated doctor brief growth on main since this story last recorded evidence: new sections now present in the brief (e.g. Host burn scan, lattice doctor health issues, Story metadata protection scan) push total bytes to 20606. The Host burn scan section in particular reads live state from the reviewing machine (~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/sessions), making this specific assertion inherently non-deterministic across machines/time in addition to being over budget right now. Net effect: the CHK-001:happy:1 manual_transcript evidence (result=pass, recorded headHash 197dc3fd) no longer reflects the current worktree state (HEAD cf8866d), and the story acceptance signal (userSees: npm test completes green) does not currently hold when re-verified.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit b9f2786fb5: brief-output smoke doctor invocations now set LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS=0 (the burn scan documented disable switch — the scan is advisory, never gates) so the 20000-byte brief budget asserts the projection deterministically instead of the operator live ~/.claude/projects/~/.codex/sessions state; budget value unchanged per excludedScope. CHK-001:happy:1 evidence re-recorded at b9f2786fb5: npm run test:brief-output green AND full npm test exit 0 from the worktree.
